check: M2: Home's scroll on the Mac, frame times
how: Release walk build (MARQUEE_WALK_BUILD="DEBUG MARQUEE_WALK", own core, arm64, app.momotus.walk) of fix/ui-ux-mac-feel with test(apple): a Mac walk measures Home's scroll; open -g -n, -MQMute YES, own -MQDataDir with Cinemeta, Rotten Tomatoes (RPDB covers), the Netflix catalog, torrent catalogs and Kitsu installed in a first launch, art cache emptied; -MQScrollWalk YES moves Home's NSScrollView 2400 pt/s to its foot (13,151 to 13,183 pt) and back, three passes, one step per 120 Hz refresh; no pointer or key sent; the Mac under other agents' load (load average 7 to 16)
result: stutter confirmed, not fixed. Pass 1 (cold art): hitch 78 to 120 ms/s, frame p95 13.7 to 20.8 ms, main-thread CPU 338 to 404 ms/s. Passes 2 and 3 (art cached): hitch 74 to 470 ms/s, p99 up to 211 ms, max up to 760 ms, CPU 388 to 506 ms/s, rising pass over pass in 4 of 5 runs. Apple's line for a smooth scroll is under 5 ms/s

check: M2: where the main thread goes while Home scrolls
how: xctrace Time Profiler and SwiftUI templates attached to the MS1 walk; main-thread samples, busy stretches of 12 ms or more
result: the app's own code is under 3 percent of the late frames (no HomeScreen or RowView body runs per step). The time is SwiftUI's lazy-stack work for the nested shelves: lazy placement and predecessor sizing (LazySubviewPlacements, LazyHVStack.lengthAndSpacing), preference combining across the lazy rows (LazyPreference, DynamicPreferenceCombiner, 43 percent of the long stretches in one trace), new tile views (makeElements, accessibility, focus and hover modifiers), the hover hit test on each step, and AppKit's own scroll step (about 50 ms/s). A navigation title on Home's stack (to stop the title preference) and an eager HStack inside each shelf were tried and made it worse (CPU 668 ms/s on pass 3); both were taken out
